newsitem.title: GERMANY: High yields indicated for German sugar beet crop.
newsitem.headline: High yields indicated for German sugar beet crop.

text.p: Germany's sugar beet crop should produce high yields, barring unforeseen weather changes ahead of harvesting from the middle of September, industry association WVZ said.
"The impression of beet numbers per hectare and of the beet's health in general is very good and points to high yields." a WVZ official said.
"The sugar content would benefit from more sun, but this may well be received in July/August."
The crop survived a severe winter without major damage and benefited from long spells of rain in the spring.
But a record sugar content figure of 18.17 percent in the 1996/97 (Oct-Jan) campaign might not be repeated.
High sugar content last year was the result of an unusual coincidence of factors, including rain in August and low pest occurrence.
WVZ has put the 1997/98 area at 508,687 hectares after 514,452 ha in 1996/97, when 26.06 million tonnes of beet were delivered and beet yields were 50.7 tonnes per ha.
This resulted in 4.20 million tonnes of sugar output, whites value.
